response.justification: The candidate brings valuable geospatial domain expertise (GISCollective, Green Map) and demonstrated experience building distributed systems at scale (Dunnhumby's millions-of-requests-per-second infrastructure). However, there is a critical gap: C++ is the primary requirement, yet his last substantial C++ work was over 10 years ago (National Instruments, 2014-2015), with recent roles focused on TypeScript/Node.js. Additionally, he lacks specific experience in navigation/routing systems, which is core to this role. His proven ability to learn multiple languages is a plus, but this combination of gaps makes him risky for a mid-senior individual contributor position in critical infrastructure.
strengths: Deep geospatial/GIS domain expertise with shipped projects (GISCollective open-source platform, Green Map web GIS application)
Proven ability to design and operate distributed systems handling massive scale (millions of HTTP requests per second at Dunnhumby with low-latency performance optimization)
Demonstrated learning agility and technical breadth across multiple languages and domains (C++, DLang, Node.js, etc.) with strong software engineering practices
concerns: C++ experience is over 10 years stale (last work: National Instruments 2014-2015); recent 5+ years focused on TypeScript/Node.js; no Rust alternative mentioned
No production experience with navigation, routing systems, or tile-based data processing; geospatial background differs significantly from routing infrastructure requirements
Recent career trajectory emphasizes product/web development (Optilyz pricing platform, re:cinq full-stack work) rather than systems/infrastructure, making domain transition less clear
